pool.text: Consider the region bounded by the curves \(y = x^2\) and \(y = 4\). This region is revolved around the line \(y = 5\) to form a solid. A cylindrical hole is drilled through the center of this solid, perpendicular to the axis of revolution. The radius of the cylindrical hole is \(r\). The volume of the material removed by the cylindrical hole is given by \(V_{\text{hole}} = \pi \int_a^b (R(x)^2 - r^2) dx\), where \(R(x)\) is the outer radius of the solid at a given \(x\) and \(a, b\) are the limits of integration. Find the value of \(a\) and \(b\), and the expression for \(V_{\text{hole}}\) in terms of \(r\). The question asks for the setup of the integral representing the volume of the material removed.

pool.sol: The region is bounded by \(y = x^2\) and \(y = 4\). To find the intersection points, we set \(x^2 = 4\), which gives \(x = \pm 2\). These are our limits of integration, \(a = -2\) and \(b = 2\). The region is revolved around the line \(y = 5\). The outer radius \(R(x)\) is the distance from the axis of revolution (\(y=5\)) to the outer boundary of the region. The outer boundary is the curve \(y = x^2\). So, \(R(x) = 5 - x^2\). The inner radius of the cylindrical hole is given as \(r\). The volume of the material removed by the cylindrical hole is the integral of the area of the annular cross-section, which is \(\pi (R(x)^2 - r^2)\). Therefore, \(V_{\text{hole}} = \pi \int_{-2}^2 ((5 - x^2)^2 - r^2) dx\).
